newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda sees bigger '97 exports to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Honda sees bigger '97 exports to U.S.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Monday it expects its car exports to the United States to jump to 240,000 units in calendar 1997.
This would be up 58 percent from the 152,000 units exported in 1996.
The increase was anticipated because of expected strong demand for the Civic model in the United States and because Honda started shipping its CR-V light sports-utility vehicles there in January.
It aims to export 60,000 CR-Vs to the United States in 1997.
In January, Honda said its U.S. sales in 1997, excluding the luxury Acura model, could hit 780,000 units, exceeding the record of 735,920 set last year.

Including the Acura, which is sold through a separate network, it expects U.S. sales to reach 900,000, up from 843,928 in 1996, while overall North American sales are expected to reach to one million units, up from 917,645 last year.
